record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: The selective nearest neighbor rule SNN is reported empirically to have average running time O(dn^3). Can one prove theoretical results giving average-case running-time bounds of this kind for SNN?

evidence.quote: Wilson and Martinez [41] and Wilson [42] claim that the average running time of SNN is O(dn3). No theoretical results along these lines are known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $S = \{(x_1, y_1), \ldots, (x_n, y_n)\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathcal{C}$ be a labeled training set, where $\mathcal{C}$ is a finite set of class labels. For a query point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and a subset $T \subseteq S$, the nearest neighbor classifier $\mathrm{NN}_T(x)$ assigns to $x$ the label of the point in $T$ whose feature vector is closest (in Euclidean distance) to $x$.

A subset $T \subseteq S$ is called consistent with $S$ if $\mathrm{NN}_T(x_i) = y_i$ for every $(x_i, y_i) \in S$. The selective nearest neighbor (SNN) rule produces a minimum-cardinality subset $T^* \subseteq S$ such that, for every $(x_i, y_i) \in S$, the nearest point of $T^*$ to $x_i$ has label $y_i$ and is at least as close to $x_i$ as the nearest neighbor of $x_i$ in $S \setminus \{x_i\}$ (so that selecting $T^*$ preserves the original $1$-NN classification on every training point).

Assume the points $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ are drawn i.i.d. from some reasonable probability distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (e.g., absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on a bounded region, with the labels generated by some measurable rule).

Problem. Prove (or disprove) a rigorous average-case complexity bound of the form
$$\mathbb{E}[\,t_{\mathrm{SNN}}(S)\,] \;=\; O(d\,n^{3}),$$
where $t_{\mathrm{SNN}}(S)$ denotes the running time of a specified algorithm that computes the SNN subset $T^*$ from $S$, and the expectation is taken over the random draw of $S$. More generally, establish theoretical average-case running-time bounds for algorithms implementing the SNN rule.
artifact.category_tag: Average-case complexity of nearest neighbor instance selection
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turn up only empirical claims of an O(dn^3) average running time for the selective nearest neighbor rule (attributed to Wilson and Martinez) and complexity results for related but distinct algorithms (e.g., FCNN, shared-NN). No rigorous average-case analysis of the SNN rule appears to be available, so the question appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Fast condensed nearest neighbor rule
status_evidence.snippet: FCNN rule has subquadratic worst case time complexity
status_evidence.claim: Complexity analyses exist for related instance-selection rules (FCNN), but not specifically for the average-case behavior of SNN.

status_evidence.title: Nearest neighbor search - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of NN search variants and complexities.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references do not record a proven average-case bound for the selective nearest neighbor rule.
